newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian state to decide Sterlite smelter's fate.
newsitem.headline: Indian state to decide Sterlite smelter's fate.

text.p: Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd expects a decision by the government of southern Tamil Nadu state in two days on the reopening of its smelter, closed due to allegations of a gas leak, a senior company official said on Friday.
"The chief minister has said that the decision will be taken in two days," K. Ranganathan, general manager (commercial), told Reuters by telephone.
Ranganathan said Sterlite had expected instructions from the government by July 31 but the government had now extended the time period.

Last month the firm was asked to halt operations at its copper smelter at the southern port of Tuticorin after suspected gas emissions reportedly caused the hospitalisation of more than 100 workers in a nearby factory.
The company strongly denied that a gas leak was responsible.
The state government set up an expert committee to examine emissions from the plant.

The Financial Express newspaper on Friday quoted Tamil Nadu chief minister M. Karunanidhi as saying the report submitted by the expert committee was "not satisfactory" and the government would decide in two days whether to allow the company to reopen its plant.
The smelter, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, began operations in December 1996.
Company officials have said the closure is costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,280) daily. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
